title: Start Here
one_liner: The plain-language front door: what We The Citizens is, in sixty seconds and then in five minutes.
scope_in: What the movement is; who it is for; the one-sentence and one-paragraph versions; a map of the rest of this site; the single call to action to app.WeTheCitizens.io.
scope_out: Any mechanism detail (how awards are computed, how evidence chains work) — those get linked, never explained here.
newcomer_question_it_answers: What is this and why should I care?

title: The Problem
one_liner: What is actually broken in democracy today, stated without jargon and without asking the reader to already agree.
scope_in: Representative democracy not working as promised; capture of institutions; the deliberate-deadlock pattern (classify a slice, then demand 100% proof); why arguing on social media changes nothing.
scope_out: Our solution — that is how_it_works. Naming specific living people — that lives in the politician areas under sourcing rules.
newcomer_question_it_answers: Why does anything need fixing?

title: The Movement
one_liner: Who We The Citizens is: the charter, the four pillars, and what joining actually means.
scope_in: Charter and vision; the four pillars in plain language; the two personas (citizen, admin); what membership costs and does not cost; the paid-supporter option; how decisions inside the movement are made.
scope_out: Product mechanics; the paired social network (see repos).
newcomer_question_it_answers: Who is behind this and what am I joining?

title: How It Works
one_liner: The core loop end to end: record a position, reason it out, decide, and optionally publish the fix.
scope_in: The six-step loop; individual mode vs community mode at a glance; what the app does for you and what it never does for you; a worked walkthrough of one real issue.
scope_out: Install steps (get_started); the internals of any single pillar (those have their own areas).
newcomer_question_it_answers: What do I actually DO with it?

title: Get Started
one_liner: Running We The Citizens: hosted at app.WeTheCitizens.io, or local-first on your own computer.
scope_in: Hosted vs localhost:4444; first-run mode selection; the movement data repo and why the app asks for it; signing in (optional on localhost); the wtcx CLI and the MCP server.
scope_out: Contributor build instructions and repo layout — those live in repos.
newcomer_question_it_answers: How do I get it running?

title: The Social Contract
one_liner: The reference standard everything is measured against — the Constitution and representative democracy as promised.
scope_in: Why a movement needs a fixed yardstick; the US social contract and how it is written down here; how other countries plug in their own; what counts as misalignment vs disagreement.
scope_out: Individual policy fights — those are decisions and problems.
newcomer_question_it_answers: Measured against WHAT? Who says you are right?

title: Problems
one_liner: The movement's ranked catalog of what is wrong, each one sourced, and open for citizens to add to.
scope_in: What a problem record is; root causes; how problems are ranked; the current catalog (Epstein files withheld, JFK records withheld, Congress exempt from its own laws, settlements paid and hidden, the economy rigged); how any citizen proposes a new one.
scope_out: Proposed legislative language that fixes a problem — that is fix_laws and good_bills.
newcomer_question_it_answers: What specific problems are you working on?

title: Laws
one_liner: The four law libraries at a glance, and the one distinction that makes them make sense: who wrote it and did anyone let it vote.
scope_in: The map of the four libraries (problem laws, fix bills, good laws, and the fixing process); the vocabulary — a law is enacted, a bill is language nobody filed; why the movement keeps them apart.
scope_out: The contents of any one library — each has its own area below.
newcomer_question_it_answers: What is the difference between a law and a bill here?

title: Problem Laws
one_liner: The enacted laws the American people did not want, were not asked about, and are governed by anyway.
scope_in: What makes a law a problem law and who approves the list; the badness rating 1 to 100 and the citizen vote on it; root causes each law creates; the frozen key and why a record never silently changes; how a citizen reports one, sources mandatory at the door.
scope_out: How a named person voted on them — that is monkey and voting_records.
newcomer_question_it_answers: Which laws are the ones actually doing the damage?

title: Fixing the Law
one_liner: Pillar 2 in practice: how a problem citizens named becomes real legislative language somebody could file tomorrow.
scope_in: The path from problem to root causes to drafted sections; the coverage matrix that shows which root causes a draft closes and which it visibly does not; packages of bills that only close the argument together; who writes them and how citizens propose a fix.
scope_out: The finished drafts themselves — those are good_bills.
newcomer_question_it_answers: How does a complaint turn into an actual law?

title: Fix Bills
one_liner: Language the movement wrote that nobody has filed — real bills, with real sections, waiting for a sponsor.
scope_in: The library of drafted fix bills; what each one does section by section; the four-bill Charlie Kirk disclosure package as the worked example; the standing rule that a fix bill is not a law and no page may imply otherwise; giving feedback on a draft.
scope_out: Bills that somebody actually filed — those are good_laws.
newcomer_question_it_answers: Do you have actual legislation, or just ideas?

title: Good Laws
one_liner: Laws and bills that would repair democracy — the ones that passed, the ones voted down, and the ones never allowed a vote at all.
scope_in: The good law list and its admission tests (repeal, restore, transparency, accountability, franchise, due process, speech, purse); the goodness rating and the citizen vote on it; the three fates of a good law; who blocked one from advancing and how that is recorded.
scope_out: The reward a politician earns for advancing them — that is llama.
newcomer_question_it_answers: Has anyone tried to fix this, and what happened?

title: Politicians
one_liner: Everything we publish about a politician is an award earned or not earned — and the wall that keeps the record separate from the resume.
scope_in: The doctrine that governs every politician page: it is an award, never a score, never a grade on a person; the wall between the in-office voting record and everything else; the four rosters and how to find yours; how a politician or their staff disputes a record.
scope_out: Each award and each roster — those are the areas below.
newcomer_question_it_answers: Are you just calling people names with extra steps?

title: Elected Politicians
one_liner: The 1,364 people who have held office and left a voting record — the hardest, most checkable evidence in the movement.
scope_in: What a legacy record contains and where every row came from; the roster and how to find who represents you; the two awards a voting record can earn; the pending to for_vote to voted lifecycle; correcting your own record if you are the subject.
scope_out: People who have never held office — that is new_politicians.
newcomer_question_it_answers: What has my representative actually done in office?

title: Good New Leaders
one_liner: The people worth electing who have never been in office — assessed on what they have said and done, not on a voting record they do not have.
scope_in: The roster of new political leaders; how somebody gets on it and who may recommend them (anyone, including a logged-out visitor); what is assessed — interviews, writing, public commitments, background; the percent-known companion; worrisome challengers and why flagging one costs sources.
scope_out: Anyone with a voting record — that is legacy_politicians.
newcomer_question_it_answers: Who should I vote FOR, not just against?

title: The Monkey Award
one_liner: One number, 0 to 100, for how much a named politician did to put the democracy-destroying laws in place. Higher is worse.
scope_in: What the award answers and the Monkey List it is computed over; the twelve categories every recorded act falls into; why blocking a repair weighs thirty floor votes; the weighted average with no curve and no cohort; why a 0 does not mean good; reproducing the number with a calculator.
scope_out: Anything outside the voting record — that never touches this award, by rule.
newcomer_question_it_answers: What does a 72% Monkey Award actually mean?

title: The Llama Award
one_liner: The mirror of the Monkey: how much a named politician did to repeal harmful law and advance the law that repairs democracy. Higher is better.
scope_in: The Good Law List and its admission tests; the same twelve categories and the same equation, one different table; why the Llama table is not the Monkey table inverted — a vote for a harmful law costs a repair record four times what it gains the damage record; dominance, which decides the award a card leads with.
scope_out: Anything outside the voting record — that is flamingo.
newcomer_question_it_answers: Does anybody get credit for doing the right thing?

title: The Flamingo Award
one_liner: Everything outside the voting record — and the only award with a state that means we have not looked yet.
scope_in: What the Flamingo covers (transcripts, interviews, background, resume, education, public commitments, qualification assessments); the three states and their marks; why full-colour, dark red and gray-brown must never collapse into one another; the award case and the per-area drill-in down to a single transcript.
scope_out: The in-office record — that is monkey and llama, and the wall keeps them apart.
newcomer_question_it_answers: How do you judge someone who has never voted on anything?

title: Voting Records
one_liner: How we read the public record of how someone voted — the source of the hardest numbers on the site.
scope_in: Where voting data comes from and how it is downloaded; what counts as a vote, an authorship, and a block; how a record becomes an award percentage; gaps and how they are shown rather than hidden.
scope_out: Assessment of people with no record — that is new_politicians and flamingo.
newcomer_question_it_answers: How do you know how they voted?

title: Qualifications
one_liner: What makes somebody worth electing — sixteen rubrics, 781 graded criteria, published in the open before anyone is assessed.
scope_in: The qualification areas (economics, anti-corruption, constitutional competence, foreign policy, citizens rights, intellectual rigor, loyalty, life experience and the rest); how a rubric is written with levels 1 to 10; why a market Democrat, an industrial-policy Republican and a deregulatory libertarian can all score a 9; reading the rubrics yourself.
scope_out: The blend that turns assessments into one number — that is meritocracy.
newcomer_question_it_answers: How do you judge without just judging by party?

title: Meritocracy
one_liner: Influence here is earned and visible: a ladder citizens climb by doing checkable work, with a hard ceiling so it can never become a hierarchy.
scope_in: The trust ladder (New, Identified, Contributing, Established, Steward); the merit score and what feeds it — a published corpus anyone can re-derive, verified actions, corroboration, tenure, and accuracy over time; the bounded 2x weight and why unbounded merit becomes oligarchy in three years; merit buys attention never authority; money and admin favour buy zero; anonymity never caps the ladder.
scope_out: The action catalog that earns the credit — that is take_action.
newcomer_question_it_answers: Who gets to decide, and how do I stop it becoming a clique?

title: Decisions
one_liner: Pillar 1: you record where you stand, the platform runs the comparison, and communities can pool the result.
scope_in: Recording a position; running the calculation against the social contract; individual position vs community consensus and the delta between them; yes/no votes and policy positions; publishing a decision.
scope_out: Value systems that drive the judgment — that is values.
newcomer_question_it_answers: How do I record what I actually think?

title: Values
one_liner: Pillar 3: turn your ethics into something an AI can apply consistently, at scale, on your behalf.
scope_in: Writing down your rules for deciding this versus that; the structured value-system format; downloading a policy packet you agree with or publishing your own; how AI applies a value system to a real issue; the limits of doing this.
scope_out: Verification of factual chains — that is evidence.
newcomer_question_it_answers: How can software possibly represent what I believe?

title: Evidence
one_liner: Pillar 4: deciding when a few links are missing on purpose — the answer to you cannot prove it so you cannot say it.
scope_in: Chain-of-evidence records; explicit gap tracking (classified, suppressed, blocked); setting your own confidence threshold for action; AI checking the chain from first principles; grading a source.
scope_out: Any claim about a living person without a source — never published, see open_data.
newcomer_question_it_answers: What if the proof is deliberately withheld?

title: Communities
one_liner: Where the work happens together: communities, the areas inside them, and the citizens doing the work.
scope_in: What a community is and how it is scoped; areas inside a community; joining, leaving, stewarding; how individual decisions aggregate into a community position; trusted citizens.
scope_out: The merit weighting inside that aggregation — that is meritocracy.
newcomer_question_it_answers: Do I have to do this alone?

title: Take Action
one_liner: The catalog of things a citizen can actually do this week, each one worth points and each one checkable.
scope_in: The action catalog across five tracks (challengers, communications, organizing, lawmaking, participation); what each action is worth, from adding a video at 5 points to a challenger winning at 5,000; how an action is logged with a URL and a description as evidence; peer reporting; anti-gaming.
scope_out: What the points become — that is karma.
newcomer_question_it_answers: What can I do today that is not just posting online?

title: Karma
one_liner: The citizen side of the ledger — raw points are noise, the monthly karma score is the record, and the history book is permanent.
scope_in: Why karma is deliberately called a score when a politician award is not; raw points to normalized monthly karma and why the month is the unit; the karma dashboard, the weekly bars and the lifetime number; verification and disputes; the leaderboard; the Leader History Book, hash-chained so it cannot be quietly rewritten.
scope_out: The menu of things that earn it — that is take_action. Politician awards — those are monkey, llama and flamingo.
newcomer_question_it_answers: What do I get out of doing the work?

title: Open Data
one_liner: The movement's public record is a git repository. Clone it, check every claim, and send back a correction.
scope_in: The data repo and how it is laid out; the sourcing rule — no claim about a living person without a source_url; provenance trails for every download; how a citizen proposes a correction and why a decline must state a reason the author can read; coverage and the gaps we publish rather than hide; what we deliberately do not collect.
scope_out: Analysis built on top of the data — those are the topic areas above.
newcomer_question_it_answers: Where does all this come from, and can I check it myself?

title: AI
one_liner: What the AI is allowed to do, what it is never allowed to decide, and the hard rules the build itself enforces.
scope_in: AI as a verifier of reasoning rather than an oracle; checking a chain from first principles; assessing transcripts against a published rubric; the advisory-only pass that never awards a point; what a human must always sign off on; the hard rules, including the one that says this codebase never downloads media, enforced by a test that fails the build.
scope_out: Value systems themselves — that is values.
newcomer_question_it_answers: Is an AI deciding my politics?

title: Repos
one_liner: Every repository, what is in it, and how to run the whole movement on your own machine.
scope_in: The repo map — the app (backend, frontend, shared, wtcx CLI, MCP server), the open data record, this website, and the paired social network; licenses; how to contribute code, data, or a correction; running your own instance; what stops us from becoming the censor.
scope_out: Using the hosted product — that is get_started.
newcomer_question_it_answers: Can I see the code, and can I fork you?

title: We The Citizens R
one_liner: The Republican front door at WeCitizensR.com: your own seats, your own incumbents, and who could replace them.
scope_in: What the WeCitizensR.com edition is and why it exists; the three-column seat block (in office, Republican challenger, strongest challenger from any other party); how the edition finds the seats you actually vote on; what this door stands for, drawn from marketing/messaging/republicans.md; the funnel into app.WeTheCitizens.io.
scope_out: Award arithmetic (monkey, llama, flamingo); the reasoning engine, values and evidence chains, which live only in the main app; anything that characterizes a party rather than a person and a vote. Nothing here is written to match another edition — there is no mirror rule.
newcomer_question_it_answers: I am a Republican — is this site for me?
